note: Missouri River bottomland south-west of Oregon, bought by the Corps of Engineers for river mitigation and managed with MDC. Camping is at the single small gravel lot at the north end, off Memphis Road on the river side of the levee: no pads, tables, toilets or water, and room for a rig or two. No open fires. The ground is river bottom that floods; the Missouri is about 500 m west across fields and timber and not in view. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: one designated camping point (map symbol + GIS point) beside the only lot - stays as a designated point at a lot. Corps-owned land managed cooperatively with MDC (ownership question). No open fires. Free/FCFS/14 nights/no hookups confirmed. Not waterfront stands. Minor pin move onto the lot. Phone matches.
flags: DESIGNATED POINT (lot rule - STAYS): page lists 'Designated Camping Sites'; brochure: 'Primitive camping is permitted only in areas identified on area map. Camping is limited to 14 consecutive days in a 30-day period.' The 7/15/2021 map legend has 'Primitive Camping' and draws the symbol directly under the area's one Parking Lot symbol at the north end. GIS layer 27: one 'Primitive Camping Area' point at 39.92958,-95.19594. (The second camping symbol on the map, at the south-east corner by the concrete boat ramp, is Payne Landing Access - already its own entry, id 13928.)

WHAT IS ON THE GROUND: a gravel lot about 15 x 30 m widening off the access track, and south of it a bare graded patch about 25 x 40 m; the GIS camping point is 55-60 m south-west of the lot in rough bottomland grass at the edge of a brushy swale, with no pad or track at it. The levee with its crown road runs 30-40 m east of the lot, so the lot is on the river side of the levee. Ground around shows pale silt - flood deposit. Nothing built.

OWNERSHIP - REPORTED, NOT CHANGED: the page: 'The United States Army Corps of Engineers has purchased this area as part of the Missouri River Mitigation Project ... The area is managed through a cooperative effort between the Corps of Engineers and the Missouri Department of Conservation.' The page carries no Rule 101 'not owned by MDC' line. Stored ownership is state (MDC manages, MDC rules and phone); the landowner is the Corps. Owner's call whether that stays state.
FIRES: brochure 'No open fires.' - in the note.

FLOODING: neither the page nor the brochure states a flood closure; the note's 'floods' rests on the lot being river bottom inside the levee with silt visible on imagery. No current notice on the page.
PIN MOVE (minor, about 85 m): stored 39.92958,-95.19594 (GIS point, in rough grass) -> proposed 39.93003,-95.19515, the gravel lot.
ACCESS: Memphis Road (gravel county road) to the levee, then the area's gravel track; brochure: 'Motor vehicles are allowed only on graveled' roads and lots. No ford, no posted limit, no 4WD wording.
WATERFRONT - NOT WATERFRONT STANDS: the Missouri River bank is about 500 m west beyond fields and bottomland timber.
PHONE: stored 816-271-3100 matches the page's 'For more information call (816) 271-3100'.
No split (one point). Nothing else in the database within 3 km (Payne Landing Access is about 3.8 km south-east).
